title: Emit provision-to-ready metrics + tracing spans (step breakdown)
author: Gabe Wilson
description: Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation sprint, we need step-level visibility into where time is spent and why nodes fail before they are marked Ready. Today we only have coarse timing at the workflow boundary, which makes it hard to separate image issues vs cluster join vs validation flakes. This PR adds standardized metrics and tracing spans for each provisioning + validation step, with observability-reviewed naming + label constraints to keep cardinality under control. What’s in this PR: (1) Metrics emitted for every step execution (provisioning + validation): fleet.provision_to_ready.step.duration_ms (histogram), fleet.provision_to_ready.step.attempts_total (counter), fleet.provision_to_ready.step.failures_total (counter), and fleet.provision_to_ready.step.inflight (gauge). (2) A top-level workflow timer: fleet.provision_to_ready.workflow.duration_ms (histogram), tagged to match step metrics so we can compare end-to-end vs sum-of-steps. (3) OpenTelemetry spans around each step with consistent naming + attributes for cross-service correlation: span name provision_to_ready.step, with attributes step.name, step.phase (provisioning|validation), fleet.region, fleet.pool_type, fleet.gpu_sku, image.channel, result (success|failure|timeout|skipped). (4) Error classification plumbing: we map raw errors into a bounded set of error_class values (e.g., kubelet_join, driver_parity, gpu_health, nccl_smoke, network, storage, unknown) so dashboards/alerts can aggregate without exploding on message text. (5) Guardrails: explicit label allowlist + runtime checks to prevent accidental high-cardinality tags (e.g., node_id/instance_id/hostname are rejected and logged at debug). Metric naming / label policy: Per Allison’s review, all metrics are under the fleet.provision_to_ready.* namespace and use histogram for durations; label keys are intentionally small and bounded. Labels used: step, phase, region, pool_type, gpu_sku, image_channel, result, error_class. NOTE: node identifiers are intentionally NOT attached to metrics; the readiness service continues to store per-node artifacts/log pointers for drill-down. How to verify: (1) Run local unit tests: go test ./... (2) Manual smoke: start a dev provisioning run and confirm spans appear under service=fleet-readiness + service=provisioning-orchestrator; verify metrics are emitted and aggregated in Prom. (3) Cardinality check: run internal load test with 200 nodes and confirm series count is stable (no node-level labels). Follow-ups: (a) ENG-4827 dashboard PR will consume these metrics; (b) SLO toolkit PR will compute time-to-ready SLIs from the readiness events, but step metrics should still be used for triage and alert enrichment.

review_conversation: Allison Grant (requested changes): Metric names should be namespaced under fleet.provision_to_ready.* and duration should be a histogram (ms). Also please remove node_id/instance_id from labels; that’s a hard no for Prom series growth. Add a small allowlist or a helper that makes it difficult to accidentally tag with hostname later.

Gabe Wilson (author): Ack. Updated metric names + switched duration to histogram. Removed node_id labels; added LabelGuard allowlist + tests that fail if node_id/hostname gets through. Also added error_class mapping so we don’t ship error_message as a label.

Aisha Bello: Can you confirm the label values are bounded? Specifically: image version vs channel. If we tag exact image version we’ll get lots of churn; would prefer channel (candidate/stable) + gpu_sku.

Gabe Wilson (author): Good call. Metrics use image_channel only; exact version stays in traces + readiness artifacts (not metrics). gpu_sku is included but comes from a fixed enum set in fleet config.
Miles Thornton: For workflow.duration_ms, does it include time spent waiting on retries/backoff? We’ll want to interpret this consistently with the SLO definition later.

Gabe Wilson (author): It includes wall-clock time from workflow start to terminal state (success/failure/quarantine), including backoff. Step.duration_ms is per attempt; attempts_total + failures_total let us see retry amplification.
Vanessa Ortiz: Please add an example query or at least confirm it’s easy to aggregate P95 by step + region. That’s the main triage view we need for rollout week.
Gabe Wilson (author): Added a short metric catalog note in README with sample PromQL (p95 by step/region) and guidance on recommended group-bys.
Benji Okafor: Minor: result label should be consistent across services (success|failure|timeout|skipped). Right now I see error vs failure in one spot.
Gabe Wilson (author): Fixed. Standardized result values and added a unit test to prevent regressions.
Allison Grant (approved): Thanks. Namespacing + label guard look good. Approved once CI is green.
Aisha Bello (approved): Approved. This should unblock the dashboard + alert work without cardinality surprises.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Gabe Wilson after approvals from Observability + SRE. No rollout flags changed in this PR; safe to ship ahead of staged rollout.
